items.stem: A private subnet instance needs to download OS updates but must not accept inbound connections. What provides this?

options.rationale: Correct: a NAT gateway allows outbound-initiated traffic while blocking unsolicited inbound.

options.text: An internet gateway attached to the subnet
options.rationale: An internet gateway would make the subnet public and allow inbound.
Peering connects VPCs; it does not provide internet egress.

options.text: A security group allowing all inbound
options.rationale: Opening inbound is the opposite of the requirement.

items.explanation: Correct: a NAT gateway allows outbound-initiated traffic while blocking unsolicited inbound.

items.stem: How do security groups differ from network ACLs in a VPC?

options.text: Security groups are stateful; NACLs are stateless
options.rationale: Correct: security groups track connection state and auto-allow return traffic; NACLs evaluate each direction.

options.text: Security groups are stateless; NACLs are stateful
Both operate only at the subnet level
options.rationale: Security groups apply to ENIs/instances; NACLs apply at the subnet.

items.explanation: Correct: security groups are stateful (return traffic auto-allowed); NACLs are stateless.

items.stem: Which TWO statements about VPC peering are correct? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Peering is not transitive between VPCs
options.rationale: Correct: traffic does not route through a peered VPC to a third.

options.text: Route tables must be updated on both VPCs
options.rationale: Correct: each VPC needs routes to the other's CIDR.
Peering connects VPCs, not on-premises sites.

items.explanation: Correct: peering is non-transitive and requires route-table entries on both sides.
